title: How long can the third side of a triangle be?
description: Two sides are given and the third side is found as a range, for the pairs one and one hundred, five and five, and three and seven. The third side lies strictly between the difference and the sum of the other two.
teaching_notes: One idea: the third side is less than the sum and more than the difference of the other two. Watch for children who give only the upper limit, or who include the end values, where the circles only touch.

source: For each of the following, give at least 5 possible values for the third length so there exists a triangle having these as sidelengths (decimal values could also be chosen): (a) 1, 100 (b) 5, 5 (c) 3, 7. See if you can describe all possible lengths of the third side in each case, so that a triangle exists with those sidelengths. For example, in case (a), all numbers strictly between 99 and 101 would be possible.
video_script.why: The child can test three lengths and now turns the test round to find every third length that works for two given lengths.
video_script.substitution: In each part two lengths are given and the third length is the unknown, written x.
video_script.anchor: Three pairs of lengths with the third length left as a question mark
video_script.payoff_line: The third length lies strictly between the difference and the sum of the other two lengths.

final_answer.value: (a) strictly between 99 and 101, for example 99.5, 100, 100.5; (b) strictly between 0 and 10, for example 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; (c) strictly between 4 and 10, for example 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
final_answer.spoken: the third length lies strictly between the difference and the sum of the other two lengths; in the first part between ninety nine and one hundred and one, in the second part between zero and ten, and in the third part between four and ten

never_show: the ranges before the answer beat
maths_rules: in general, with lengths p and q, |p - q| < x < p + q
video_script.design: One idea: the third length lies between the difference and the sum of the other two. The three pairs stay in the anchor band; the working band holds the board solution.

beats.on_screen: three pairs of strips: 1 and 100; 5 and 5; 3 and 7, each with a third strip marked by a question mark
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
Three pairs of lengths are given, and each needs a third length.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which third lengths make a triangle?

beats.on_screen: the pairs and the question marks stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a base with two circles whose radii are the two given lengths; the third length x shown as the base

marks.circles: two circles appear with the given lengths as radii
marks.base: the base x is marked, with the circles crossing above it

beats.colours: circle at A in blue, circle at B in orange
narration: <bookmark mark='circles'/>Think of two circles whose radii are the two given lengths.
<bookmark mark='base'/>The third length is the base, and the circles must cross above it.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the pairs are one and one hundred; five and five; and three and seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: all possible values of the third length x
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find every possible value of the third length.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: x < sum of the other two; the larger given length < x + the smaller
narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step one, the third length must be less than the sum of the given two.
<bookmark mark='low'/>The larger given length must be less than the third length plus the smaller one.

marks.a2: 100 < 1 + x is written and becomes x > 99

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Step two, take one and one hundred. The third length is less than one plus one hundred, which is one hundred and one.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>One hundred must be less than one plus the third length.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>That makes the third length more than ninety nine.

marks.b2: 5 < 5 + x is written and becomes x > 0

narration: <bookmark mark='b1'/>Step three, take five and five. The third length is less than five plus five, which is ten.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>Five must be less than five plus the third length.
<bookmark mark='b3'/>That makes the third length more than zero.

marks.c2: 7 < 3 + x is written and becomes x > 4

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step four, take three and seven. The third length is less than three plus seven, which is ten.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Seven must be less than three plus the third length.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>That makes the third length more than four.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: for lengths p and q: difference of p and q < x < p + q

marks.rule: the three ranges are joined into one rule with the difference on the left and the sum on the right

beats.colours: difference in blue, sum in orange
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step five, for any two lengths, the third lies strictly between their difference and their sum.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step six, check the first part with ninety nine point five.
<bookmark mark='ok'/>The longest is one hundred.
One plus ninety nine point five is one hundred point five, which is more.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (a) strictly between 99 and 101, for example 99.5, 100, 100.5; (b) strictly between 0 and 10, for example 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; (c) strictly between 4 and 10, for example 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The third length lies strictly between the difference and the sum of the other two lengths.
<bookmark mark='r1'/>In the first part, it is between ninety nine and one hundred and one.
In the second part, it is between zero and ten.
<bookmark mark='r3'/>In the third part, it is between four and ten.
